title: Dun Morogh
body: Dun Morogh is the snowbound heart of Khaz Modan, a high country of frozen lakes, pine forests and wind-scoured ridges, walled in by mountains and reached only through a few passes kept by dwarven mountaineers. It is the homeland of the Ironforge dwarves, whose great city is carved into the mountain at its heart, and of the gnomes, whose city of Gnomeregan lies beneath the western hills. The Frostmane ice trolls once ruled these snows, until dwarven armies broke their empire and drove them into the hills, and they trouble the dwarves still. Now worse troubles have come. Troggs have poured out of the deep places, seizing the Coldridge tunnel and the Gol'Bolar Quarry, and Gnomeregan itself was lost, its halls poisoned and its people scattered across the land. With much of King Magni's army fighting far away beside the Alliance, mountaineers, Senate envoys and any stout-hearted volunteers must hold the line.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dun_Morogh_(Classic) (snowy region, Khaz Modan mountains on all sides, passes guarded by dwarven troops, home of gnomes and dwarves)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Frostmane_tribe (once ruled Dun Morogh, empire fell to dwarven armies, retreat to the hills)
quest 3361 description (gnomes scattered all over Dun Morogh)
quest 314 description (King Magni's army off fighting with the Alliance)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Removed the unsupported claim that brewers hold the line; softened 'raid' to 'trouble'.

title: Coldridge Valley
body: Coldridge Valley is a sheltered vale in the southwestern corner of Dun Morogh, where young dwarves and gnomes take their first steps as defenders of Khaz Modan. Wolves and crag boars roam its snowfields, and the hunter Talin Keeneye keeps a camp beside the frozen lake. The valley is far from peaceful. Frostmane trolls hold a cave at its southern end, and the Senate envoy Grelin Whitebeard camps in the valley to weigh the threat they pose. Rockjaw troggs have spread across the southeastern hills, even overrunning a dwarven camp to the west. The gnome Felix Whindlebolt, fleeing the ruin of Gnomeregan, found refuge here only to have the trolls carry off his belongings.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Coldridge_Valley (southwestern corner, dwarf and gnome start before Cataclysm)
quest 233 description (Talin's camp by the frozen lake)
DB spawns in area 132: Ragged wolves, Small Crag Boar, Rockjaw Trogg, Frostmane Troll Whelp, Grik'nir 808
quest 182 description (Grelin sent to investigate the troll threat)

title: Anvilmar
body: Anvilmar is a dwarven settlement dug into the mountainside at the northern edge of Coldridge Valley, the first place of any size a newcomer to the valley will find. Around its great forge, trainers of many callings instruct new recruits, and merchants sell arms, armor and warm clothing. Durnan Furcutter swears there is nothing like a cup of scalding mornbrew on a chilly Dun Morogh day, though Nori Pridedrift, who brings it up from Grelin Whitebeard's camp, fears no cup will reach him before it runs cold. The gnome Felix Whindlebolt has sheltered here since fleeing Gnomeregan, though he grumbles that the place holds as many nasty creatures as his old home did before the accident.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Anvilmar (northern Coldridge Valley, first settlement of significance, large forge, class trainers)
quest 3364 description (a settlement dug into the mountain)

title: Coldridge Pass
body: Coldridge Pass is the tunnel linking Coldridge Valley with the rest of Dun Morogh, and the troggs have claimed it. Rockjaw raiders lurk along its length and fall on anyone passing through, and Mountaineer Thalos keeps watch at the valley end, asking travelers with no pressing business to stay in Anvilmar until the way is safer. Since the troggs overran the pass, scarcely any word from Anvilmar has reached Kharanos. Near the tunnel mouth the gnome Hands Springsprocket waits with a crate of supplies for the inn at Kharanos, unable to cross until a mountaineer escort comes through, and glad to hand it to any hardy traveler bound that way.
sources: DB spawns in area 800: Rockjaw Raider 1718, Mountaineer Thalos 1965, Hands Springsprocket 6782, Coldridge Mountaineers
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Kharanos
body: Kharanos is the bustling heart of Dun Morogh, a dwarven town nestled among the peaks on the road north to Ironforge. It has a large forge and a gnomish workshop, and its pride is the Thunderbrew Distillery, where Innkeeper Belm invites travelers to fill a tankard and pull up a chair. Mountaineers guard its roads, and recruits who come up through the Coldridge tunnel continue their training here. Kharanos is also where Senir Whitebeard, envoy of the Senate, keeps an eye on the Frostmane trolls, and where the gnomes Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket labor over a machine they believe can cure the leper gnomes of Gnomeregan.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Kharanos (bustling town among the peaks, large forge, gnomish workshop, Thunderbrew Distillery, recruits from Anvilmar train there)

title: Thunderbrew Distillery
body: The Thunderbrew Distillery is the most famous building in Kharanos, tavern, inn and brewery in one, and the home of Thunder Ale. Ragnar Thunderbrew presides over the taps. Down in the cellar, Jarven Thunderbrew guards the barrels under strict orders not to touch a drop, though he admits a taste of Thunder Ale would sharpen his wits. The Thunderbrews guard their recipes jealously, and with reason. Dark Iron dwarves have already stolen the family's recipe for Thunderbrew Lager, and the rival Barleybrews of Brewnall Village would dearly love to see their own Scalder served to Thunderbrew patrons in place of the house ale.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Thunderbrew_Distillery (famous dwarven tavern in Kharanos with inn and trainers)
DB: Ragnar Thunderbrew 1267 and Jarven Thunderbrew 1373 in Kharanos; gameobjects 269/270 Thunder Ale barrels

title: Steelgrill's Depot
body: Just northeast of Kharanos stands Steelgrill's Depot, the shop of Beldin Steelgrill, reckoned the best siege engine mechanic there is and notoriously hard on his tools. It is a favorite haunt of veteran siege engine pilots, and Pilot Stonegear and Pilot Bellowfiz trade boasts about their machines while they wait on his repairs. Milli Featherwhistle sells mechanostriders from the yard and Binjy Featherwhistle teaches gnomes to ride them, and Loslor Rudge keeps the engineers supplied.
sources: DB spawns in area 189: Milli 7955 and Binjy Featherwhistle 7954 (mechanostriders), Gnomeregan Trainee 39349, Disassembled Mechano-Tank 39263, Captain Tread Sparknozzle 39675
quest 25285 description (mechano-tanks readied for the assault)
notes: Converted for eras: the Operation: Gnomeregan preparations moved to part 1 (minState 13, no trigger), since the event and its spawns were added in patch 3.3.5 and do not belong to classic Dun Morogh. creature_text 1377, 1378 and npc_text 4253 reread: nothing from later builds. Mechanostrider line made specific (Milli is the merchant, Binjy the riding trainer). The Operation: Gnomeregan quests here cannot be started on this server (25229 has no starter and gates 25199 and 25285), so only the visible preparations are mentioned; those NPCs are permanent phase 1 spawns.

parts.body: Of late the depot has grown crowded. Gnomeregan trainees stand in ranks in the yard, and beside Captain Tread Sparknozzle a row of half-assembled mechano-tanks waits to be readied and tested, for the exiles of Gnomeregan are preparing machines and recruits for an assault to take back their city.
sources: DB spawns in area 189: Gnomeregan Trainee 39349 (12, in ranks), Disassembled Mechano-Tank 39263, Captain Tread Sparknozzle 39675, all phase 1
quest 25285 description (mechano-tanks readied for the assault)

title: The Grizzled Den
body: The Grizzled Den lies in the snowy hills west of Kharanos, the lair of a band of wendigo. These shaggy brutes make the surrounding slopes dangerous: a courier hauling a crate of ammunition for the gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot was chased off near the den and fled without his cargo. Their thick manes are prized all the same, and Pilot Stonegear wants a heap of them as a rug for the deck of his siege engine. South of the den, snowfields teem with crag boars and bears, hunted for meat and fur by those who supply the depot.
sources: quest 313 description (Grizzled Den, west of Kharanos)
quest 317 description (snow fields south of the Grizzled Den)

title: Chill Breeze Valley
body: Chill Breeze Valley is a stretch of wild country west of Kharanos, roamed by wendigo and big crag boars. Here Tundra MacGrann keeps a lonely camp and hunts deer in spite of a bad leg. He had salted away a month of dried meat for the cold season in a thorium locker, safe from bears, but while he was off hunting, the great wendigo Old Icebeard carried the whole locker away to its cave. Too slow on his bum leg to slip in and out of the lair, MacGrann faces a hungry winter unless someone retrieves his stash. A wendigo known as Edan the Howler also prowls the valley.
sources: DB spawns in area 801: Old Icebeard 1271, Tundra MacGrann 1266, gameobject 272 MacGrann's Meat Locker, Wendigo, Large Crag Boar, Edan the Howler 1137

title: Brewnall Village
body: Brewnall Village stands on the west bank of Iceflow Lake, west of Kharanos, home of the Barleybrew family. Rejold Barleybrew is on a quest to brew the perfect stout and will try any ingredient, even the shimmerweed the Frostmane trolls grow for their rituals. Some of his brews taste good, some bad, and some, like the fiery Evershine, would lay all but the stoutest dwarf flat. Marleth Barleybrew nurses a rivalry with the Thunderbrews of Kharanos. Bears, snow leopards and old crag boars wander close to the village, and the brewers would gladly see them thinned so they can get on with their crafting and brewing.
sources: quest 287 description (Brewnall Village on the west bank of Iceflow Lake)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Brewnall_Village (home of the Barleybrews, protect the village from wild animals)

title: Iceflow Lake
body: Iceflow Lake is the frozen lake of western Dun Morogh, reached by following the frozen river west from the bridge on the road north of Kharanos. Brewnall Village stands on its western bank, and Frostmane Hold lies in the hills beyond. Along its shore the Ganters keep a fishing camp, with Paxton Ganter teaching the trade and Gretta Ganter selling fishing supplies. Winter wolves hunt the snows around the lake, some of them gaunt and starving, and a great wolf called Timber is sometimes seen among them.
sources: DB spawns in area 211: Paxton Ganter 1700 (Fishing Trainer), Gretta Ganter 8508 (Fishing Supplies), Winter Wolf 1131, Starving Winter Wolf 1133, Timber 1132

title: Frostmane Hold
body: Frostmane Hold is the stronghold of the Frostmane ice trolls, a cave in the hills southwest of Brewnall Village. Their empire once spanned Dun Morogh, until the dwarves broke it and drove the survivors into the hills, a shameful blow to so warlike a people. Headhunters, hideskinners and shadowcasters crowd the Hold in such numbers that Senir Whitebeard, who found it, did not dare go inside. Great Father Arctikus, patriarch of the tribe, walks the snows around it, and in the foothills just to the south stands the hut of Vejrek, said to be the toughest troll in these parts.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Frostmane_tribe (empire fell to dwarven armies, shameful blow to their warlike nature, Frostmane Hold their capital, Arctikus patriarch)
quest 1678 description (Vejrek's hut south of Frostmane Hold)

title: Shimmer Ridge
body: Shimmer Ridge rises in the hills east of Brewnall Village, where the Frostmane trolls grow shimmerweed, a plant they use in their strange tribal rituals. Frostmane seers tend the crop and store it in baskets, with snowstriders and headhunters standing guard, and they have no patience for outsiders after their harvest. The dwarves have found little use for the weed, but its unique taste has caught the fancy of Rejold Barleybrew of Brewnall Village, who is eager to try it in his brews.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Frostmane_tribe (grew shimmerweed on Shimmer Ridge for rituals)

title: Gnomeregan
body: In the western hills of Dun Morogh lies the surface entrance to Gnomeregan, once the capital of the gnomes. When troggs invaded from below, the gnomes fought back with a radiation purge that went horribly wrong, poisoning their own city and killing or twisting a great many of its people. The survivors scattered across Dun Morogh or fled to Ironforge. The land before the gates now belongs to leper gnomes, their minds clouded by sickness, some so addled that they take any stranger for a trogg. Irradiated trogg looters prowl near the entrance, and a few evacuees still try to slip away.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Gnomeregan (trogg invasion, radiation plan, heavy losses, refugees to Ironforge, entrance in western Dun Morogh)

title: Amberstill Ranch
body: Amberstill Ranch lies on the eastern road toward Loch Modan, where the Amberstill family breeds the sturdy rams that carry the dwarves of Ironforge. Veron Amberstill will hand the reins of a ram only to a proven ally of Ironforge, and Ultham Ironhorn teaches riders to handle them. Yarlyn Amberstill spends the days chasing a rabbit called Fluffy, who wants no part of a bath. The herd has a deadly enemy in Vagash, a wendigo who lurks on the slopes above the ranch and picks off rams in the night, and with most of King Magni's army away with the Alliance, Rudra Amberstill has no soldiers to call on.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Amberstill_Ranch (north of Gol'Bolar on the road to Loch Modan, rams, Vagash a Wendigo)

title: Gol'Bolar Quarry
body: Gol'Bolar Quarry is a great dig site in southeastern Dun Morogh, worked by Ironforge's miners until they dug too deep. Troggs poured out of the earth, wrecked the equipment and drove the miners from their own pit, and now Rockjaw skullthumpers and bonesnappers swarm the workings while the dwarves hold a camp at the rim. Foreman Stonebrow of the Miners' League watches his blasting powder go up in smoke and rages for revenge, and Senator Mehr Stonehallow has come in person to see the quarry cleared and the miners back at work. In the shadier corners of Ironforge, some whisper that the king is stripping the quarry of ore and gems.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Gol%27Bolar_Quarry (dig site in southeastern Dun Morogh, troggs took over, Miners' League)
quests 2238, 2239 (Hidden Circle claims about the King strip mining the quarry)

title: Helm's Bed Lake
body: Helm's Bed Lake is a small frozen lake in southeastern Dun Morogh, and its shores are no place to linger. Rockjaw troggs, from ambushers to backbreakers, crowd its banks, and scarred crag boars roam the surrounding hills. South of the lake lies something the dwarves like even less. Dark Iron dwarves have bunkered down in an old compound there, and two dwarves who crept close enough to spy on them saw their leader giving orders to his men before more of the Dark Irons caught them by surprise.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Helm%27s_Bed_Lake (small lake in southeastern Dun Morogh, Dark Irons in an abandoned building to the south)
DB spawns in area 212: Rockjaw Ambusher 1116, Backbreaker 1118, Bonesnapper 1117, Skullthumper 1115, Scarred Crag Boar 1689
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. The spies being caught is the premise of quest 1783, told on accepting it. verified

title: Ironband's Compound
body: South of Helm's Bed Lake stands the compound of Sturgy Ironband, a master blacksmith who once taught his craft to students here. One day a student brought him a load of strange ore, which Ironband called umbral ore and was eager to work. Soon after it arrived, a band of Dark Iron dwarves attacked the compound and killed everyone inside. The Dark Irons hold it still, their spies and their captain, Beld, falling on any who come near. Narm Faulk, a dwarf of the Light, fell nearby while spying on them, having stayed behind so that his companion could escape and fetch help.
sources: DB spawns in area 716: Dark Iron Spy 6123 x12, Captain Beld 6124, Narm Faulk 6177, gameobject 85562 Ironband's Strongbox
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. The massacre is the premise of quest 1681, and Narm Faulk's body is plain to see; his rescue (quests 1783 to 1785) is not told. verified

title: North Gate Outpost
body: North Gate Outpost is one of the two dwarven guard towers watching the passes from Dun Morogh into Loch Modan, held by mountaineers. In the hills nearby, Pilot Hammerfoot of the Siege Brigade stands guard over the engines he and his friend Mori Hildelve drove here in search of a rare ore needed for high-grade blastpowder. Hildelve wrecked his engine on a steep slope and went on searching alone, on foot. That was days ago, and he has not come back. Since then Hammerfoot has heard beastly growls in the hills at night, and he is starting to worry.
sources: quest 413 description (one of two towers on the border to Loch Modan)
DB spawns in area 808: Pilot Hammerfoot 1960, Mangeclaw 1961, gameobject 2059 A Dwarven Corpse, Dun Morogh Mountaineers
notes: Converted: Hildelve's death and Mangeclaw as his killer moved to part 1 on the turn-in of 419 (at the corpse). The opening keeps him missing, as quest 419 presents it. Mangeclaw's death is told in 133 part 2. verified

parts.body: Hildelve lies in the snow not far from the engines, mauled, frozen and picked clean by mountain scavengers, his Brigadier's Vest still on him and his journal clutched in his hand. In it he wrote that a huge ice claw bear called Mangeclaw attacked him. He drove the beast off, but it came back to finish him, and his last wish was revenge.
sources: DB: gameobject 2059 A Dwarven Corpse in area 808

title: South Gate Outpost
body: South Gate Outpost is the southern of the two guard towers on Dun Morogh's border with Loch Modan, where mountaineers watch over the tunnel that leads southeast toward Thelsamar. Its best known sentry is Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew, brother of the brewer Rejold. He is no brewer like the rest of his family, but he loves his drink, and he grumbles that he has not had a good fight in days and his barrel of ale is nearly dry.
sources: quest 413 description, completion and reward text
quest 414 description (southeast through the tunnel to Thelsamar)
DB spawns in area 806: Mountaineer Barleybrew 1959, Dun Morogh Mountaineers
notes: Converted: Wellart's verdict on the Shimmer Stout moved to part 1 on the turn-in of 413, where he tastes it. verified

parts.body: A barrel of his brother's new Shimmer Stout has reached the tower, and one taste put a shine in Wellart's eyes. He swore he could see in the dark. He liked it so well that he kept on drinking it, and soon wanted a fellow mountaineer, Kadrell, who patrols the road through Thelsamar, to try it as well.

title: Grelin Whitebeard
body: Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were sent by the Senate of Ironforge to weigh the threat the trolls pose to Dun Morogh, and Grelin made his camp in Coldridge Valley. The Senate has its hands full with the troggs and wants no further annoyances. From what Grelin has seen, the Frostmane here are poorly placed, mostly confined to the valley's southern cave, and he judges that the army will not be needed when a few strong arms will serve. He has the authority to pay those who lend them, and he is always glad of mail, since word from Ironforge comes to his camp but rarely.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Frostmane_tribe (the Senate sent Grelin and Senir Whitebeard)
notes: Converted: the stolen journal moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 182, whose reward text reveals it); the journal's return, his verdict and the trusted courier moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 218). The king's name line (quest 420 reward text, Senir's words) left to Senir's entry 121 part 1 and story 130 part 3, since Grelin's own triggers never reach it. Mail line added from quest 234 reward text. Faction 1: Grelin uses faction 55 (Ironforge) and quest 234 is Alliance only. Check: added part 3 (QUEST_DONE 420) so the King's name line from the original is not lost from Grelin's own entry; dropped 'having learned his lesson' (not in quest 282).

parts.body: The trolls answered in the night. A group of them crept into Grelin's camp and stole his journal, the notes his report depends on, and carried it off to their cave. The one who had it was a big brute with odd markings on his skin and face, and Grelin, fuming, mutters that he knew better than to trust his good-for-nothing apprentice.

With his notebook back, Grelin declares the troll situation in Coldridge Valley under control and not much cause for worry. He puts the finishing touches on his report for Senir, and he will not leave it to his apprentice: he wants it carried in more reliable hands through the trogg-infested tunnel to Kharanos.

Grelin's report leans on the King's name, though Senir had told him to be sparing with it. When it reaches Kharanos, Senir judges it sure to ruffle some feathers in the Senate, and is not sorry: those feathers, he says, needed ruffling.

title: Senir Whitebeard
body: Senir Whitebeard, Grelin's brother and a special envoy of the Senate, works out of Kharanos, sent to look into the threat the Frostmane trolls pose to Dun Morogh. He is a sociable soul who would sooner share a drink than tramp through the snow, there being little else to do in the cold, and he freely admits he has fallen behind on his report, blaming the bloody cold. It was Senir who found where the trolls are holed up, at Frostmane Hold, though the sheer numbers he saw there kept him from going in.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Senir_Whitebeard (special envoy of the Senate of Ironforge, Kharanos)
notes: Converted: his view of Grelin's use of the King's name moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 420, which stays an entry trigger too); his finished report and the request to keep quiet moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 287, after which 291 is offered). Redstone's reaction is told in story 130 part 4. Faction 1: Senir uses faction 55 (Ironforge).

parts.body: When Grelin's report reaches him, Senir reads it with a grin. He told his brother to be sparing with the King's name, but Grelin did not listen. It is sure to ruffle some feathers in the Senate, Senir admits, though in his view those were feathers that needed ruffling, and it reminds him that his own report is overdue.

Once the Hold has been scouted, Senir scribbles out his report at last, laughing at something in it, and sends it to Senator Barin Redstone, a sour sort who waits in the chamber in Ironforge where King Magni holds court. He asks only that no one mention how much help he had: the Senate must not think he is idle out here.

title: Senator Mehr Stonehallow
body: Senator Mehr Stonehallow sits in the Senate of Ironforge and belongs to the Explorers' League, yet he has left the city to take charge of the trogg problem at the Gol'Bolar Quarry himself. He has no illusions about the troggs. As the miners dug deep, the creatures poured out, smashed the equipment and drove everyone away, and he sees nothing to do but exterminate them. His plan is plain: clear the pit, bring in mountaineers to hold it, rebuild and put the miners back to work, the first step of many against an infestation gripping the dwarven lands.
sources: quest 433 description, completion and reward text
DB spawn: Senator Mehr Stonehallow 1977 at Gol'Bolar Quarry
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. His plan is what he says on offering quest 433; the quarry being cleared is told in 131 part 2. Faction 1: faction 55 (Ironforge), quest 433 Alliance only.

title: Rejold and Marleth Barleybrew
body: The Barleybrews of Brewnall Village are a family of brewers, and Rejold Barleybrew is their restless genius, sure that brewing is in his blood and the perfect stout within his reach. He will experiment with anything, from troll-grown shimmerweed to the fiery Evershine that one siege pilot throws into his engine's furnace for a burst of power. Marleth Barleybrew grudgingly admits the Thunderbrews make good drinks, but means to teach them theirs is not the only decent brew, even if it takes a barrel of Barleybrew Scalder smuggled into the Thunderbrew cellar. Rejold's brother Wellart, no brewer at all, serves as a mountaineer on the Loch Modan border.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified. Faction 1: both use faction 55 (Ironforge). Marleth's exact kinship to Rejold is not stated, so the text only calls the Barleybrews a family of brewers.

title: Ragnar Thunderbrew
body: Ragnar Thunderbrew presides over the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos and is fiercely proud of the family recipes, from Thunder Ale to his famous Beer Basted Boar Ribs, whose secret, he swears, is in the malt. Supplies have been harder to come by since his trapper went off to join the king's army at the Alliance front. Ragnar has a temper. When Dark Iron dwarves led by Hurley Blackbreath stole the family recipe for Thunderbrew Lager, he swore they were in for it, and he will reward any champion willing to turn Blackrock Depths upside down to bring it back.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. The stolen lager recipe is the premise of quest 4126; its return is not told. Faction 1: faction 55 (Ironforge).

title: Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket
body: Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket are gnomish inventors working out of Kharanos with one goal: to undo what Gnomeregan's radiation did to their people. Their grand project is the Recombobulator, a machine meant to reverse the leper affliction, which they test on a captured leper gnome with mixed results and endless adjustments. Ozzie is also working on a cure made from the green glow of irradiated troggs, though by his own admission it might just turn out to be a very powerful rum. He was standing beside Gnoarn on the day a radiation bolt took all of Gnoarn's hair.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ozzie_Togglevolt (working on a cure for leper gnomes with Razzle)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Removed 'friend' (quest 2927 only says Ozzie stood next to Gnoarn). Faction 1: both faction 875 (Gnomeregan Exiles).

title: Pilot Stonegear and Pilot Bellowfiz
body: Two veteran siege engine pilots pass the time at Steelgrill's Depot, waiting on Beldin Steelgrill's repairs and arguing about everything. Pilot Stonegear drives 'Trollplow', a heavily armored engine whose battle scars he wears with pride, and he scoffs at any design that sheds armor to save weight. Pilot Bellowfiz would rather race the circuit than fight in the arena, and swears a splash of Evershine in the furnace of his 'Jetsteam' has carried him out of more than one tight spot. Stonegear wants wendigo manes for a rug, while Bellowfiz is stocking up for a long mission for the Siege Brigade.
sources: quest 400 reward text (repairs on Stonegear's siege engine)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Faction 1: both faction 55 (Ironforge).

title: Felix Whindlebolt
body: Felix Whindlebolt is one of the gnomes scattered across Dun Morogh when Gnomeregan was lost. As he tells it, the gnomes drove the troggs out of their city, and then it all went horribly wrong, leaving their home completely irradiated. Felix fled in such haste that he lost all his belongings and tools, and the Frostmane trolls carried off his chest, his box and his bucket of bolts to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. No adventurer, he waits in Anvilmar, convinced the place is no fit home for the likes of him, and gloomily observes that things are not looking good for Felix.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. npc_text 15139 (gossip 10898) reread: a generic line, nothing resting on later events. Faction 1: faction 875 (Gnomeregan Exiles), quest 3361 Alliance only.

title: Grik'nir the Cold
body: Grik'nir the Cold leads the Frostmane trolls who hold the cave at the southern end of Coldridge Valley, a band Grelin Whitebeard thought too poorly placed to need the army. A big brute with odd markings on his skin and face, he keeps to the cave among the troll whelps and novices of his band, far from Frostmane Hold, the tribe's stronghold in the western hills.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Grik%27nir_the_Cold (Frostmane Hovel at the southern end of Coldridge Valley)
DB spawns in area 132: Grik'nir 808, Frostmane Troll Whelp 706, Frostmane Novice 946
quest 182 description (trolls mostly in the southern cave, army not needed)
notes: Checked: the journal theft moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 218, whose text names him as the one who has it), since the KILL trigger alone tells nothing of it. Removed the northward push against outlying camps (wiki framing that matches the Cataclysm valley, not quest 182); Cataclysm fire elemental plan left out. Faction 0: the KILL trigger is open to both factions.

parts.body: It was Grik'nir and a group of his trolls who crept into Grelin's camp in the night and made off with the dwarf's journal, the notes his report to the Senate depends on. Grik'nir keeps it with him in the cave, and Grelin wants it back.

title: Great Father Arctikus
body: Great Father Arctikus is the patriarch of the Frostmane tribe, the ice trolls who ruled Dun Morogh before the dwarves broke their empire. He carries the Frostmane Scepter and wears the Royal Frostmane Girdle as marks of his station, and he walks the snows around Frostmane Hold, the tribe's stronghold in the western hills. Any stranger who intrudes there is told plainly that defiling Frostmane Hold will cost a life. To the dwarves he is a reminder that the Frostmane, though driven into the hills long ago, still follow a leader of their own.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Frostmane_tribe (former patriarch and great leader; Frostmane Scepter, Royal Frostmane Girdle)
DB spawns: Great Father Arctikus at Frostmane Hold (area 135) and nearby
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Faction 0: KILL trigger, hostile to all.

title: The Whitebeard Reports
body: With its hands full of troggs, the Senate of Ironforge wants no further annoyances, so it sent the brothers Grelin and Senir Whitebeard to weigh the threat the Frostmane trolls pose to Dun Morogh. Senir works from Kharanos, while Grelin camps in Coldridge Valley. From what Grelin has seen, the trolls of the valley are poorly placed, mostly confined to the southern cave, and he judges the army unnecessary: a few strong arms should be more than enough. He has the authority to pay for them, and once the trolls are dealt with he means to write up his findings for the Senate.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 182. Parts follow the chain: 1 the stolen journal (QUEST_DONE 182), 2 the journal's return and the courier (QUEST_DONE 218), 3 Senir on the King's name and the Hold (QUEST_DONE 420), 4 Redstone's fury (QUEST_DONE 291). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only (AllowableRaces 1101) except 282, which still sits inside the Alliance chain. 182 is the only entry point; 287 requires 420. Check: part 2 names Grik'nir again, as the original did.

parts.body: The trolls answered by night. A group of them crept into Grelin's camp, stole his journal and carried it off to their cave, the one who had it a big brute with odd markings on his skin and face. Without those notes there could be no report.

Once the journal was won back from Grik'nir the Cold, Grelin declared the valley's trolls under control and finished his report. Trusting it to no apprentice, he sent it in reliable hands through the trogg-infested tunnel, past Mountaineer Thalos, to his brother Senir in Kharanos.

Senir read it and laughed. He had warned his brother to be sparing with the King's name, and the report leaned on it heavily, sure to ruffle feathers in the Senate. Behind on his own work, Senir first needed Frostmane Hold scouted, the troll stronghold southwest of Brewnall Village that he had found but not dared to enter.

With the Hold scouted, Senir finished his report and sent it to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge, asking that no one mention how much help he had. Redstone read it and exploded. Authority of the King! Had Magni taken leave of his senses, and had Whitebeard taken matters into his own hands? The Senate, he warned, would not be pleased, not one bit.

title: The Trogg Menace
body: Troggs have burst out of the deep places of Khaz Modan, and all of Dun Morogh feels it. In Coldridge Valley, Balir Frosthammer reports them across the southeastern hills and by the frozen lake, and only nights ago they overran a dwarven camp to the west. They hold the tunnel to Kharanos so firmly that supplies and news have all but stopped, and the gnome Hands Springsprocket must ask passing travelers to carry a crate through to the inn. At the Gol'Bolar Quarry they poured out of the diggings, wrecked the equipment and drove off the miners. Foreman Stonebrow rages as his powder barrels go up one by one, while Senator Mehr Stonehallow, who has taken this part of the infestation upon himself, sees nothing to do but exterminate the troggs, rebuild and put the miners back to work.
notes: Converted: Balir's fears after the valley fight moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 170); the quarry cleared and the plan to hold it moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 433). The opening now gives Stonehallow's plan as he states it on offering 433. Faction 1: all four quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Driving the troggs back in Coldridge Valley brings Balir little comfort. If the troubles there are any sign of what is happening elsewhere in the dwarven lands, he says, there are hard times ahead, and he can only hope that the king and the Senate are taking steps against the threat.

At Gol'Bolar the troggs are thinned at last. It is a start, Stonehallow allows, and only the first of many steps that must be taken against this menace. Next he hopes to move mountaineers in to secure the quarry, then restore the works and get the miners digging again.

title: Barleybrew and Thunderbrew
body: Brewing is serious business in Dun Morogh. In Brewnall Village, Marleth Barleybrew admits the Thunderbrews of Kharanos make good drinks, but means to teach them that theirs is not the only decent brew. The plan is to slip a barrel of Barleybrew Scalder into the Thunderbrew Distillery's cellar in place of their Thunder Ale, and see how the patrons like it. The cellar guard, Jarven Thunderbrew, is under orders not to touch the ale, which is exactly why a mug of it makes such a fine distraction. Rejold Barleybrew, meanwhile, is on a quest for the perfect stout. He wants shimmerweed, which the Frostmane trolls grow on the ridge to the east for their rituals, sure that its unique taste belongs in his next batch.
notes: Converted: the switch and Marleth's satisfaction moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 310 at the barrel, or 311); the Shimmer Stout and Wellart's verdict moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 413); Kadrell's verdict moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 414; 414 is sorted under Dun Morogh, QuestSortID 1, and no Loch Modan entry uses it). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only. 308 is auto-complete and only available while 310 is active, so it is not a trigger. Check: part 1 trigger narrowed to QUEST_DONE 311, since Marleth's reaction is only told at that turn-in, not at the barrel (310).

parts.body: The switch is made. A barrel of Barleybrew Scalder now sits among the Thunderbrew barrels in the distillery cellar, dated to be tapped soon, and a barrel of Thunder Ale goes back to Brewnall Village as proof of the deed. Marleth is well pleased, and reminds anyone in need of a stout with a kick not to forget the Barleybrews.

The shimmerweed worked. Rejold threw it into a batch he had nearly ready, and the result was his new Shimmer Stout. A barrel went to his brother Wellart, a mountaineer at the South Gate tower who is no brewer but loves his drink. One taste put a shine in Wellart's eyes, and he swore he could see in the dark.

Wellart liked it so well that he kept drinking, and soon sent a cask on to a fellow mountaineer, Kadrell, who patrols the road through Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Kadrell tasted it and swore by Magni's beard: the stout set his head turning and lightened his limbs, until he felt he could fly.

title: Pilots of the Siege Brigade
body: Steelgrill's Depot draws the pilots of the Ironforge Siege Brigade, and their errands send helpers all over Dun Morogh. It begins with a crate of tools for Beldin Steelgrill, who broke his last fang-ratchet in the middle of repairs on Pilot Stonegear's engine. Stonegear wants wendigo manes from the Grizzled Den to carpet 'Trollplow', while Pilot Bellowfiz stocks 'Jetsteam' with boar meat and bear fur for a month-long mission, plus a cask of Rejold Barleybrew's Evershine to burn in its furnace. Far to the east, Pilot Hammerfoot guards the engines while his friend Mori Hildelve searches the hills on foot for a rare ore for blastpowder. Days have passed with no word, and something growls in those hills at night.
notes: Converted: Hildelve's death and his journal moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 419, at the corpse); Mangeclaw's death and Hammerfoot's thanks moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 417). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only. 400 starts with Tharek Blackstone in Kharanos.

parts.body: Hildelve is found frozen in the snow, mauled and picked clean by scavengers, his journal clutched in his hand. In it he tells of being attacked by Mangeclaw, a huge ice claw bear. He drove the beast off, but it must have come back to finish him, and his last written wish was plain: revenge on Mangeclaw.

When Mangeclaw falls, the news brings Hammerfoot only grim comfort. Hildelve was a good friend, and he wishes he could have been there when the beast was found. The deed, he promises, will be remembered by the pilots of the Ironforge Siege Brigade.

title: The Recombobulator
body: Gnomeregan's fall cost the gnomes more than a home. The attempt to purge the troggs not only failed but turned much of their own people into mindless, hostile leper gnomes. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket mean to set it right. Their Recombobulator needs Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears, salvaged from the very lepers who roam outside the city gates, and Razzle tinkers endlessly with a captured leper who seems less than thrilled. Ozzie pursues a second cure, drawn from the green glow of irradiated troggs, though it may yet turn out to be a very powerful rum. Gnoarn of Ironforge, who lost a magnificent head of hair to a radiation bolt and has thought of nothing but cleansing Gnomeregan since, sends helpers his way.
notes: Converted: the failed first test and the call for fallout from inside Gnomeregan moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2926, after which 2962 is offered). The rum line added to the opening from quest 2926's description. Entry triggers unchanged, including ACCEPT 2927, shared with ironforge.json as a known old overlap. creature_text 1269 and 5568 reread: nothing from later builds. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only (412, 2927 AllowableRaces 1101). 2927 starts with Gnoarn in Ironforge; 2926 requires it. Check: part 1 trigger changed from QUEST_DONE 2926 to QUEST_ACCEPT 2962: the 2926 turn-in only starts the test, and the failure is told in the 2962 offer (no script reveals it at the turn-in).

parts.body: Ozzie is sure of his new formula. If it works, he declares, the captured leper will be cured and he himself will have a full head of hair again. It does not work. The sample proves too small and too impure, the troggs not irradiated enough, so Ozzie demands fallout taken straight from the slimes, lurkers and horrors deep within Gnomeregan itself.
